cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 10th District since 2015 (the 11th District until 2023). Former restaurant owner and probation officer. Served on the Concord City Council (mayor in 1993), as Contra Costa County Supervisor, in the state Assembly and in the state Senate. Born in Lowell, Massachusetts; lives in Concord.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3, the National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from him on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and charters. No controversies or foreign-government ties turned up in the pages we could read. The campaign site's issues page was cut off partway through, so we left out anything beyond what was visible. We could not confirm from a primary source why he moved to California; the reason given by Wikipedia is not corroborated elsewhere in our sources.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Jeff Frese
cands.bio: Republican small business owner from Moraga running for California's 10th Congressional District in 2026. He says he founded the snack brand Fat Snax and sold it, and now runs a skincare company. He says he previously worked in product leadership at CNN, Nickelodeon and MTV. He has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: His campaign site lists these endorsements: Steve Hilton, Contra Costa Republican Party, Alameda County Republican Party, Carl DeMaio's Reform California, Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC, BAJC-Action (Bay Area Jewish Coalition), and CRPA PAC. The list is self-reported.
Ballotpedia lists the Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide (Sway voting group) as a voter guide recommendation.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jeff Frese was born or raised, or when he moved to California. We found no independent reporting confirming his business history (Fat Snax, the skincare company, or his roles at CNN, Nickelodeon and MTV); it comes from his own survey answers and campaign site. He has held no public office, so there is no record of official actions. We found no stated positions from him on H-1B visas, abortion, gun laws, homestead property taxes, a statewide data-center ban, or school vouchers and teacher pay. His campaign site lists endorsements from gun-rights and taxpayer groups, but we found no statement from him on those topics. He says he supports no federal income tax on teachers, which is not the same as a teacher pay raise.
